## Jane Austen Sentiment Analysis 

```{r}
library(janeaustenr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidytext)
library(tidyr)
library(textdata)

tidy_books <- austen_books() %>%
  group_by(book) %>%
  mutate(
    linenumber = row_number(),
    chapter = cumsum(str_detect(text, 
                                regex("^chapter [\\divxlc]", 
                                      ignore_case = TRUE)))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, text)
```

```{r}
nrc_joy <- get_sentiments("nrc") %>% 
  filter(sentiment == "joy")

tidy_books %>%
  filter(book == "Emma") %>%
  inner_join(nrc_joy) %>%
  count(word, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(tidyr)

jane_austen_sentiment <- tidy_books %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments("bing")) %>%
  count(book, index = linenumber %/% 80, sentiment) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sentiment, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>% 
  mutate(sentiment = positive - negative)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(jane_austen_sentiment, aes(index, sentiment, fill = book)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~book, ncol = 2, scales = "free_x")
```

# Citation for the above code

Silge, Julia, and David Robinson. 2017. Text Mining with R: A Tidy Approach. O'Reilly Media.

Original code: <https://www.tidytextmining.com/sentiment>

# Load Giants ESPN Articles

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)

giants_talent <- read_lines("Jaxson_Dart_all_angles .txt")
giants_injury <- read_lines("dart_knee_surgery.txt")
```

#  Tokenize the Articles

```{r}
giants_text <- tibble(
  article = c(
    rep("Talent", length(giants_talent)),
    rep("Injury", length(giants_injury))
  ),
  text = c(giants_talent, giants_injury)
)

giants_tidy <- giants_text %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, text)
```

# Identify Positive and Negative words

```{r}
giants_bing <- giants_tidy %>%
  inner_join(get_sentiments("bing"), by = "word")

giants_bing %>%
  count(article, sentiment)
```

# Sentiment Metrics

```{r}
giants_sentiment <- giants_bing %>%
  count(article, sentiment) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sentiment,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(sentiment_score = positive - negative)

giants_sentiment
```

# Visualize

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(giants_sentiment,
       aes(x = article, y = sentiment_score, fill = article)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Sentiment Analysis of ESPN Giants Articles",
    x = "Article",
    y = "Sentiment Score (Positive - Negative)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  guides(fill = "none")
```

# Using Vader (lexicon) for Sentiment 

```{r}
library(vader)

giants_vader <- vader_df(c(
  paste(giants_talent, collapse = " "),
  paste(giants_injury, collapse = " ")
))

giants_vader <- giants_vader %>%
  mutate(article = c("Talent", "Injury")) %>%
  select(article, compound, pos, neg, neu)

giants_vader
```

# Comparing Vader and Bing

```{r}
sentiment_comparison <- giants_sentiment %>%
  select(article, bing_score = sentiment_score) %>%
  left_join(
    giants_vader %>%
      mutate(vader_net = pos - neg) %>%
      select(article, compound, vader_net),
    by = "article"
  )

sentiment_comparison
```

# Discussion and Findings

The sentiment analysis shows that both ESPN articles contain more positive than negative language. Using the Bing lexicon, the article discussing Jaxson Dart's talent received a sentiment score of +57, compared to +7 for the article discussing his injury.

VADER produced similar findings, with positive-minus-negative scores of 0.121 for the talent article and 0.017 for the injury article. Both methods suggest that the talent article contains more positive language.

One limitation is that the articles may differ in length, which affects raw Bing scores. Additionally, sentiment analysis does not always capture the full context of sports journalism.
